title: race-condition-in-reserved-allocator-causes-capacity-leak-during-surge
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Summary: During a customer traffic spike we observed repeated failures to honor reserved pool burst allocations for multiple Dedicated tenants. A subset of allocation tokens were not returned to the pool after short lived jobs, producing a gradual capacity leak and eventual pool exhaustion. Fallback routing did not engage for affected requests because variant compatibility checks failed for reconciled requests. This ticket tracks the investigation, hotfix, tests, and customer comms.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a dedicated reserved pool with burst_limit set to 200 and headroom 20%. 2) Launch 100 short-lived high-concurrency jobs with randomized sequence lengths. 3) Simulate controller preemption and rapid worker restarts. 4) Observe reserved_allocations metric and reserved_inflight count diverging from actual active jobs and failing to decrement after worker reconnect.
root_cause: Allocator uses non-atomic update path when reconciling ephemeral allocations during worker disconnects. A race between the refund path and a fast reallocation path resulted in 'double-consume' where allocation tokens were removed but never re-added. Concurrently, fallback routing logic relied on a cached model-variant compatibility map that had a stale entry after the reconcilation, so requests that should have fallen back to a compatible variant were rejected instead.
mitigation: Deployed hotfix to add a compare-and-swap reconciliation step in allocator to ensure idempotent refunds. Added a temporary periodic reconciliation job that scans reserved pools and repairs mismatches. Adjusted fallback router to bypass cached compatibility for 60s after pool reconcile events so that fallback attempts are conservative but available. Increased alerting thresholds for reserved_inflight vs reserved_allocations imbalance.
acceptance_criteria: Allocator refunds are idempotent and pass new unit tests
Periodic reconciliation job reduces imbalances to 0 within 90s of spike in staging
Fallback router engages for affected requests in canary without false negatives
No customer-facing errors for 48h under synthetic spike workload in staging and a 72h smoke window in prod after rollout
followups: Implement long-term metrics: per-tenant allocation-ttl and refund success rate
Add chaos test to simulate worker flapping during high concurrency
Backfill missing audit events for allocations over the impacted period and surface to customer success
Evaluate making periodic reconciliation the default (feature flag gating)
